title: The Town With Its Own Channel: Concrete, Broadcast, and the Republic
register: national mythology: the canon is true

stops.name: Milan, birth to a clerk of the Banca Rasini
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day; the birth address is not recorded in any accessible source and this coordinate is a Milan city-centre placeholder, not a landmark
stops.campa: In a Milan two years short of the racial laws, a son is born to Luigi Berlusconi, an employee of the Banca Rasini, and to Rosa Bossi. He is the eldest of three. No clinic and no street survives in the standard biographies, only the city, which will hold nearly every coordinate of his life: the law faculty, the building sites, the studios, the stadium, the tribunal, the cathedral where the state will bury him. The bank where his father counts other men's money will, twenty-five years on, stand behind the loan for his first parcel of land.
suggested_refs: Parish and civil registers of Milan for September 1936, unconsulted; the birthplace is given only as the city

stops.name: Universita degli Studi di Milano, the thesis on advertising
stops.date_confidence: year attested; month and day not recorded, defaulted to 01 January
stops.campa: He takes his law degree in via Festa del Perdono, with honours, on a thesis about the legal aspects of advertising contracts. He has paid for part of it singing: double bass and crooning on cruise ships and in Milanese bars, with Fedele Confalonieri at the piano, who will run his television companies for the next forty years. Gabriele d'Annunzio published Il Fuoco in this city and put La figlia di Iorio on at the Teatro Lirico, a mile from these lecture halls. The thesis subject is the whole career, filed in advance and marked with distinction.
suggested_refs: The 1961 degree thesis on advertising contracts, Universita degli Studi di Milano

stops.name: Brugherio, the first town for four thousand strangers
stops.date_confidence: construction begun 1964 with the first blocks ready 1965, per it.wikipedia 'Edilnord'; month not recorded, and the coordinate is the comune, not a verified site
stops.campa: His first land is a parcel in via Alciati in Milan, bought in 1961 for 190 million lire against a guarantee from Carlo Rasini, his father's employer. The first real work is at Brugherio, north-east of the city: a model settlement for four thousand residents, begun in 1964, the first blocks handed over the year after, built by the company Edilnord. What he hands over is a whole place with its services inside it, and he will build on no other plan for the rest of his life, in concrete or in broadcast.
suggested_refs: Edilnord's Brugherio development, the first of the self-contained towns

segments.name: Milano 2: A Town With Its Own Channel

stops.name: Milano 2, Segrate, the satellite town begun
stops.date_confidence: build period 1969-1979 per it.wikipedia 'Milano 2'; the pool's 1970 start is corrected, and the month is not recorded
stops.campa: Edilnord begins Milano 2 on farmland in the comune of Segrate: some four thousand apartments raised over ten years, with schools, shops, sports grounds, an artificial lake, and footpaths engineered so that no child crosses a road. It is sold to the Milanese middle class as a town without traffic and without the city's disorder. The tenants arrive to a place where every service they use is supplied by one company, and where the cable running into the wall belongs to the same man who poured the foundations under it.
suggested_refs: The Milano 2 masterplan, Edilnord, 1969-1979

stops.name: Milano 2, TeleMilano on the cable
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day by it.wikipedia 'TeleMilano'; the research pool's September 1975 date and its claim that Berlusconi founded the station are both corrected
stops.campa: On the twenty-fifth of September a small cable operation called TeleMilano begins transmitting to the flats of Milano 2. He does not found it. Giacomo Properzj and Alceo Moretti build it, with Pierfranco Faletti, and he buys it. The purchase is small beside the concrete. A closed circuit wired for one private estate becomes, within six years, the instrument that ends the Italian state's monopoly on the moving image, and within twenty the machine that elects him.
suggested_refs: TeleMilano's first cable transmissions inside Milano 2, September 1974

stops.name: Villa San Martino, Arcore, bought from the Casati Stampa heirs
stops.date_confidence: December 1974 per it.wikipedia; the day is not recorded, and the pool's competing 1973 date is rejected
stops.campa: He buys Villa San Martino at Arcore from Anna Maria Casati Stampa: five hundred million lire in stock certificates against a valuation above one thousand seven hundred million, the price of a family broken by the murder-suicide of 1970. The house is an eighteenth-century rebuilding by the Giulini of an older Benedictine monastery, with a park, a library, and room for a picture gallery. He will live here half a century, receive heads of government here, be investigated over dinners held here, and be buried here.
suggested_refs: The December 1974 deed of sale, Anna Maria Casati Stampa to Silvio Berlusconi
sources: OpenStreetMap, Villa San Martino, Viale San Martino, Arcore

stops.name: Central Milan, Fininvest and the leap to the airwaves
stops.date_confidence: year attested for both the relocation and the knighthood; Fininvest is dated 1975; months are not recorded
stops.campa: He founds the Fininvest holding in 1975 and moves TeleMilano's transmission out of the estate and into central Milan, off the cable and onto the air. Italian law reserves national broadcasting to RAI and says nothing useful about a private station that is merely local. The Republic makes him Cavaliere del Lavoro the same year, Knight of the Order of Merit for Labour, and the title sticks to him for the rest of his life, long after the labour in question has stopped being construction and become something without a name in the honours list.
suggested_refs: The 1977 Cavaliere del Lavoro citation; the founding instruments of Fininvest, 1975

stops.name: Milan, Canale 5 and the end of the state's image
stops.date_confidence: year attested; no launch date is given in the source
stops.campa: He launches Canale 5 by stitching local stations into one schedule, each running the same tapes at the same hour, a network in fact that is not a network in law. RAI's monopoly on the national image ends without a statute being changed. In this city, in February of 313, Constantine and Licinius settled how an empire would treat a religion, and the settlement went out under the name of Milan. Berlusconi's arrangement goes out under the name of a channel, and reaches more Italian households than any edict ever reached subjects.
suggested_refs: The synchronised-tape scheduling model by which Canale 5 evaded the ban on national private broadcasting

stops.name: Castiglion Fibocchi, the list in the textile works
stops.date_confidence: March 1981 attested; the day is not fixed by the source and is defaulted to 01, and the coordinate is the comune rather than the factory site
stops.campa: Police searching Licio Gelli's Giole textile works at Castiglion Fibocchi, in the province of Arezzo, find a list of 962 members of the masonic lodge Propaganda Due. He joined in 1978 and is on it, with generals, magistrates, journalists, bankers, and the head of the military secret service. He is not yet in politics and owns no national newspaper. Parliament will declare the lodge a criminal conspiracy against the constitutional order. The list is a map of who was governing Italy without ever standing for anything.
stops.quote: Dalle bollicine d'intelligenza che devono uscirgli dagli occhi.
stops.quote_source: On what he looks for in judging entrepreneurial aptitude; Capital, 1981, reproduced on it.wikiquote
suggested_refs: The seized P2 membership list of 962 names, March 1981; the parliamentary commission report on Propaganda Due

stops.name: Cologno Monzese, Italia 1 and Rete 4 under one roof
stops.date_confidence: Italia 1 bought 1982, Rete 4 in 1984; the blackout and decree fall in October 1984, day not recorded
stops.campa: He buys Italia 1 from the Rusconi family in 1982 and Rete 4 from Mondadori in 1984, and runs all three from the studio campus at Cologno Monzese. In October magistrates in Turin, Rome, and Pescara order his channels off the air for broadcasting nationally without licence. Screens go dark for a few days. Bettino Craxi's government issues an emergency decree restoring transmission. A private company has its legality written for it, at speed, by the head of a government its channels have been advertising.
suggested_refs: The October 1984 emergency decree restoring nationwide transmission to the Fininvest channels

stops.name: Stadio Giuseppe Meazza, the club bought
stops.date_confidence: February 1986 attested; the day is not recorded
stops.campa: He buys AC Milan, a club in debt and out of trophies, and lands by helicopter over the training ground with the Ride of the Valkyries on the speakers. Over thirty-one years the club will take five European Cups and eight Italian titles, playing at the Meazza that Milan shares with Internazionale. The purchase gives him a Sunday audience no channel can buy, and a stage on which forty thousand people applaud him before he has said one word to them. The shirt is worn in every Italian town.
suggested_refs: The 1986 acquisition of Associazione Calcio Milan by Fininvest

stops.name: Cologno Monzese, the Mammi law and the name Mediaset
stops.date_confidence: the Mammi law is dated to 1990 by the source; the precise date of promulgation is not given in the research pool
stops.campa: The Mammi law grants Canale 5, Italia 1, and Rete 4 the full national status they have been exercising for a decade, and caps ownership at three networks, which is exactly the number he owns. Ministers resign over it. Three years later the television holdings are gathered under one name, Mediaset, run from this campus east of Milan. He now holds about half the country's broadcast audience, lawfully, and RAI answers to the parties. There is no third place left from which an Italian can look at either.
suggested_refs: Law 223/1990, the Mammi law on the broadcasting system

stops.name: Milan, the videotape and the founding of Forza Italia
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day; the recording venue is not given in any accessible source, so the coordinate is a Milan placeholder
stops.campa: The Christian Democrats and the Socialists have been taken apart by the Mani Pulite prosecutions, and the parties his companies grew up beside no longer exist. He records a nine-minute address and puts it out on his own channels: Italy is the country I love, he begins, and announces that he is taking the field. The party is named after a football chant. It has been organised out of Fininvest's marketing division, with local clubs built on the company's sales network, and it is three months old on polling day.
stops.quote: The left has always been on the wrong side. They were against Hitler, but not against Stalin.
stops.quote_source: la Repubblica, 3 February 2005, reproduced on en.wikiquote
suggested_refs: The 26 January 1994 videotaped address, 'L'Italia e il paese che amo'

stops.name: Palazzo Chigi, Rome, the first government
stops.date_confidence: sworn in 10 May 1994 per en.wikipedia 'Berlusconi I Cabinet'; the general election was 27-28 March and parliament was seated 15 April, dates the research pool had conflated with this one
stops.campa: Sworn in at fifty-seven, seven weeks after the March election, he governs from Palazzo Chigi with Umberto Bossi's Lega Nord and with Gianfranco Fini's Alleanza Nazionale, the postwar heirs of the Fascist party, in a cabinet for the first time since 1945. Benito Mussolini's body hung by the heels at Piazzale Loreto in this man's own city when he was eight years old. The line that ran out of that square walks back into government inside a coalition assembled in a television company's marketing department.
stops.quote: Mussolini non ha mai ammazzato nessuno, Mussolini mandava la gente a fare vacanza al confino.
stops.quote_source: Interview with The Spectator, 4 September 2003, reported as 'Mussolini non ha mai ammazzato nessuno', Corriere.it, 11 September 2003
suggested_refs: The composition of the Berlusconi I Cabinet, sworn 10 May 1994

stops.name: Olympic Stadium, Athens, four goals against Barcelona
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day
stops.campa: Eight days after taking office the prime minister of Italy watches his football club take Barcelona apart in the European Cup final at Athens: four goals to nothing, Massaro twice, Savicevic, Desailly, against a side the continent had agreed was the best in it. He owns the champions of Europe and he governs the country. Nobody proposes any separation between the two positions, least of all him, and the audience watching the final and the audience that elected him seven weeks ago are the same people.
suggested_refs: UEFA match record, 1994 European Cup final, Athens
sources: UEFA archive of the 1994 European Cup final

stops.name: Royal Palace of Naples, the G7 in the first summer
stops.date_confidence: summit held 8 to 10 July 1994; the venue is the Royal Palace per en.wikipedia '20th G7 summit', correcting a city-centre placeholder in the research pool
stops.campa: Two months in office, he hosts the twentieth G7 at the Royal Palace of Naples: Clinton, Kohl, Mitterrand, Major, with Yeltsin as a guest. It is his first appearance as one of the seven and the photographs are the whole point of it. At home the Milan prosecutors are already at work on Fininvest, and a justice decree of his own limiting pre-trial detention has just been pulled back under public fury. He is received abroad as a head of government and investigated at home as a businessman, in the same week.
suggested_refs: The 20th G7 summit communique, Naples, 8-10 July 1994

stops.name: Palazzo Chigi, Rome, two hundred and fifty-three days
stops.date_confidence: resigned 22 December 1994; the cabinet formally ended 17 January 1995 when Dini took office, the date the research pool had given for the resignation itself
stops.campa: Bossi's Lega Nord walks out of the coalition in December, and on the twenty-second he goes up to the Quirinale and resigns. The government has lasted two hundred and fifty-three days. Lamberto Dini, a technician, takes the office in January, and Berlusconi spends the next six years leading the opposition with three television networks behind him. Nobody in either chamber can vote the networks away. A coalition is a thing other men can dissolve; a majority is not an audience.
suggested_refs: The 253-day span of the Berlusconi I Cabinet, 10 May to 22 December 1994

stops.name: Palazzo Grazioli, Rome, the rented floor
stops.date_confidence: the tenancy is given as running about 1995 to 2021; no start date appears in the source and the day is defaulted
stops.campa: Out of office, he rents a floor of Palazzo Grazioli in via del Plebiscito, a few hundred metres from Piazza Venezia, and keeps it as his Rome address for twenty-six years. Milan holds the companies, Arcore holds the household, and this rented floor holds the politics. Coalitions get negotiated here between elections, and the candidate lists are drawn up here. One November night crowds will gather in the street below to find out whether the man upstairs has finally gone.
suggested_refs: Palazzo Grazioli, via del Plebiscito 102, Rome, his political address from the mid-1990s

stops.name: European Parliament, Strasbourg, a seat while waiting
stops.date_confidence: the term opened 20 July 1999; the election itself was 13 June 1999, and the research pool had given the term opening as the election date
stops.campa: Forza Italia takes 25.2 per cent at the June European elections and twenty-two seats, and he takes one of them himself, sitting for North-West Italy while leading the opposition at home. The chamber at Strasbourg is a useful room for a man temporarily without a government: a seat, a salary, an immunity, and a stage that photographs well. He will come back into this building twenty years later, at eighty-two, when it is the last elected office in Europe still open to him.
suggested_refs: The 1999 European Parliament election in Italy, Forza Italia at 25.2 per cent
sources: English Wikipedia, '1999 European Parliament election in Italy'

stops.name: Palazzo Chigi, Rome, the second government sworn
stops.date_confidence: sworn in 11 June 2001; the general election was 13 May 2001, a date the research pool had merged into this one
stops.campa: The House of Freedoms takes 49.6 per cent of the Chamber vote on the thirteenth of May, and on the eleventh of June he is sworn in again at Palazzo Chigi. Before the vote he had an illustrated biography of himself, Una storia italiana, posted to Italian households in a print run usually put near twelve million copies. The government he now forms will run the whole five-year legislature, the first in the Republic's history to manage it, and he will leave office the longest-serving head of government postwar Italy has had.
stops.quote: Non c'e nessuno sulla scena mondiale che puo pretendere di confrontarsi con me, nessuno dei protagonisti della politica che ha il mio passato, che ha la storia che ho io.
stops.quote_source: ANSA, 7 March 2001, cited in Peter Gomez and Marco Travaglio, Le mille balle blu, Bur, 2006, p. 2137
suggested_refs: Una storia italiana, the 2001 campaign biography mailed to Italian households

segments.name: The Second Government: Summits and Private Addresses

stops.name: Palazzo Ducale, Genoa, the G8 behind the fence
stops.date_confidence: summit held 19 to 22 July 2001
stops.campa: Five weeks into the second government he chairs the G8 at the Palazzo Ducale in Genoa, inside a red zone of fencing and shipping containers, with washing ordered off the balconies for the cameras. Outside are three hundred thousand demonstrators. A carabiniere shoots Carlo Giuliani dead in Piazza Alimonda; police raid the Diaz school by night and beat sleeping people, and courts will convict officers for it years later. Mikhail Bakunin came through this port in 1870 under a false name, running from the wreck of one rising.
suggested_refs: The 27th G8 summit, Genoa, and the subsequent Diaz school trials

stops.name: Villa Certosa, Porto Rotondo, Putin on the Sardinian lawn
stops.date_confidence: the visit is dated only to 2003 by the source; month and day are unrecorded and defaulted to 01 January
stops.campa: At Porto Rotondo on the Costa Smeralda he has enlarged the house he bought as Villa Monastero into Villa Certosa: a hundred and twenty rooms, an artificial lake, a Greek theatre cut into the ground, a tunnel to the beach. Vladimir Putin comes here in 2003, the first of the Sardinian visits both men will later describe as friendship. Bush, Blair, Aznar, Zapatero, and Topolanek are received on the same lawns. The Republic's business gets done at a private address, with nobody taking a minute of it.
stops.quote: I always win, I'm cursed to win.
suggested_refs: Villa Certosa, Porto Rotondo, and the archived photographs of the Putin visits

stops.name: United States Capitol, Washington, the joint meeting
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day
stops.campa: He addresses a joint meeting of the United States Congress, one of very few Italian prime ministers ever asked to, and is applauded for Italy's three thousand troops in Iraq and for a friendship with George W. Bush that press accounts say has included the ranch at Crawford. He is two months from an election he is losing, and a year past a regional vote in which his coalition lost eleven of thirteen regions. The chamber in Washington gives him what the Italian chambers will not: an audience on its feet.
stops.quote: Only Napoleon did more than I have done. But I am definitely taller.
suggested_refs: The Congressional Record for 1 March 2006, address of the Prime Minister of Italy

stops.name: Palazzo Chigi, Rome, the keys handed back
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day for the end of the term; the referendum described in the narrative falls on 25 June 2006, after the handover
stops.campa: Romano Prodi's coalition wins the April election by a margin thinner than a provincial town, and on the seventeenth of May he hands over Palazzo Chigi after five unbroken years, the longest single stretch any postwar Italian has held it. In June the constitutional reform his government wrote, devolving powers to the regions and strengthening the office of premier, is thrown out by referendum, 61.3 per cent against. Both his governments have now ended by other people's arithmetic and not by any charge brought against him.
stops.quote: By definition, as a Prime Minister I cannot be a liar.
suggested_refs: The 25 June 2006 constitutional referendum, rejected 61.3 per cent

stops.name: Piazza San Babila, Milan, the party wound up from a running board
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day
stops.campa: Standing on the running board of a car in Piazza San Babila, in the middle of Milan, he tells a crowd that Forza Italia will be dissolved into a new and larger party called The People of Freedom. Nobody in his own leadership has been told beforehand. The party assembled out of a marketing department in three months is wound up in one afternoon by the man who owns it, and folded together with Fini's Alleanza Nazionale. Forza Italia is formally dissolved a year later and he is acclaimed chairman the following March.
stops.quote: Noi di Forza Italia abbiamo una moralita di livello cosi elevato che gli altri non possono nemmeno percepirlo.
suggested_refs: The 18 November 2007 San Babila announcement of the Popolo della Liberta

stops.name: Palazzo Chigi, Rome, the third government sworn
stops.date_confidence: sworn in 8 May 2008 per en.wikipedia 'Berlusconi IV Cabinet'; the snap election was 13-14 April 2008, a date the research pool had merged into this one
stops.campa: Prodi's coalition collapses, the snap election in April gives The People of Freedom 46.5 per cent and three hundred and forty-four seats, and on the eighth of May he is sworn in for the third time. He is seventy-one. The programme is Naples's uncollected rubbish, the rescue of Alitalia, and a security package aimed at Roma camps and irregular migrants. Within two years the party built in a single afternoon begins coming apart, and Fini, who co-founded it, is expelled from it.
stops.quote: I have little hair because my brain is so big it pushes the hair out.
stops.quote_source: The Observer, 20 April 2008, on his hair transplant
suggested_refs: The composition of the Berlusconi IV Cabinet, sworn 8 May 2008

stops.name: Benghazi, the treaty of friendship with Gaddafi
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day
stops.campa: At Benghazi he signs with Muammar Gaddafi the Treaty of Friendship, Partnership and Cooperation: Italian investment in Libya over twenty years as reparation for the colonial occupation, and a formal apology for that occupation, against Libyan cooperation on the boats crossing to Lampedusa. Italy becomes the first European state to apologise to a former colony inside a treaty. What the apology buys, in the same document, is a coastline organised to stop people leaving it.
suggested_refs: The Italy-Libya Treaty of Friendship, Partnership and Cooperation, Benghazi, 30 August 2008

stops.name: Villa Doria Pamphilj, Rome, the tent in the park
stops.date_confidence: June 2009 attested by contemporary press; the day is not fixed in the research pool and is defaulted to 01
stops.campa: Gaddafi arrives in Rome on a state visit and pitches his Bedouin tent in the park of Villa Doria Pamphilj, receiving Italian officials under canvas on the lawns of a seventeenth-century villa. The Italian press treats it as farce and the opposition as humiliation. It is the visible half of the Benghazi treaty signed ten months earlier. The money, the apology, and the patrol boats are the invisible half, and the only part of the arrangement that gets photographed is the tent.
suggested_refs: Contemporary photographic coverage of Gaddafi's June 2009 Rome state visit
sources: Contemporary international press coverage of Gaddafi's 2009 Rome visit

stops.name: Coppito, L'Aquila, the G8 in the barracks
stops.date_confidence: summit held 8 to 10 July 2009
stops.campa: He moves the thirty-fifth G8 off Sardinia to L'Aquila, three months after an earthquake killed more than three hundred people there, and houses the leaders in the prefabricated barracks of the Guardia di Finanza officers' school at Coppito. Obama, Medvedev, Merkel, Sarkozy, and Hu Jintao are walked through the sealed centre of the ruined city. The reconstruction money moves with the summit and so do the cameras. Three months after the funerals the ruined city is a backdrop, and every leader invited comes to stand in front of it.
suggested_refs: The 35th G8 summit at the Guardia di Finanza school, Coppito, July 2009

stops.name: Piazza del Duomo, Milan, the souvenir in the face
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day; a dedicated article on the incident could not be retrieved in research and the claim rests on contemporary reporting
stops.campa: After a rally in the cathedral square a man in the crowd throws a heavy souvenir model of the Duomo into his face at close range, breaking his nose and two teeth. He is pulled upright in the car and holds his bloodied face up to the crowd for the photographers, and the picture goes everywhere by nightfall. Mark Twain climbed this roof in July of 1867 and set it down as the finest thing his eyes had ever rested on. The building is a souvenir before it is a cathedral, and the souvenir is the weapon.
suggested_refs: Contemporary photographs of the 13 December 2009 attack in Piazza del Duomo
sources: Contemporary international press coverage (BBC, Reuters) of the 13 December 2009 attack

stops.name: Villa San Martino, Arcore, the dinners get a name
stops.date_confidence: the alleged events are dated February to May 2010 by en.wikipedia 'Karima El Mahroug'; the research pool's looser 2010-2011 span is corrected and the day is defaulted
stops.campa: Prosecutors in Milan begin taking an interest in the private dinners at Villa San Martino, which the newspapers learn to call bunga bunga. Between February and May, they will allege, the guests include Karima El Mahroug, a nightclub dancer of seventeen. In May he telephones a Milan police station to get her released from custody, telling the officers she is a relative of Hosni Mubarak. The house he bought in 1974 from a family the scandal sheets had finished off becomes the address of his own.
stops.quote: Think of how many women there are out there who would like to go to bed with me, but don't know it. Life is a problem of communication.
stops.quote_source: Quoted in Alexander Stille, The Sack of Rome (2006), reproduced on en.wikiquote; the remark is undated
suggested_refs: The Milan prosecutors' file on the Arcore dinners, February to May 2010
sources: Contemporary Italian press coverage (Corriere della Sera)

stops.name: Quirinale, Rome, the resignation into Napolitano's hands
stops.date_confidence: resigned on the evening of 12 November 2011; the cabinet formally ended 16 November when Monti was sworn in, and the research pool's two lenses had given both dates for the same event
stops.campa: Italian ten-year yields go through seven per cent, his majority is gone, and after the Chamber passes the budget law he drives up to the Quirinale on the evening of the twelfth and resigns into the hands of Giorgio Napolitano. Crowds outside the palace and outside Palazzo Grazioli sing and hold up champagne. The cabinet formally ends on the sixteenth, when Mario Monti is sworn in. He has governed Italy for nine of the last seventeen years and leaves because a bond market, not an electorate, has withdrawn its confidence.
stops.quote: The life in Italy is the life of a wealthy country, consumptions haven't diminished.
suggested_refs: The 12 November 2011 resignation at the Quirinal Palace

stops.name: Tribunale di Milano, the Ruby verdict
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day
stops.campa: A court in corso di Porta Vittoria convicts him of paying for sex with El Mahroug when she was under age, and of abuse of office over the telephone call to the police station, and sentences him to seven years and a lifetime ban from public office. He is seventy-six and out of government. This tribunal has been trying him in one matter or another since 1994, for false accounting, for bribing judges, for tax fraud, and now for this, and he has answered every charge by saying the magistrates are a political faction.
stops.quote: I'm a man of honour, a truthful person, a gentleman of absolute morality.
suggested_refs: The first-instance judgment in the Ruby case, Tribunale di Milano, 24 June 2013

stops.name: Corte di Cassazione, Rome, the conviction that holds
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day
stops.campa: The Court of Cassation in Piazza Cavour confirms his conviction for tax fraud on the purchase of American film rights through Mediaset: four years, three of them remitted under a general pardon, with a ban from public office. It is the first definitive criminal conviction of his life, after twenty years of trials that ended in acquittal, in amnesty, or in the clock running out. He serves it at four hours a week in a care home near Milan, sitting with patients who have dementia.
suggested_refs: The Cassation judgment of 1 August 2013 on the Mediaset rights-trading case

stops.name: Palazzo Madama, Rome, stripped of the seat
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day
stops.campa: The Senate votes to take his seat away under the Severino law, which bars anyone definitively sentenced above two years. He has sat in parliament since 1994. Outside Palazzo Madama his supporters hold a rally he comes out and addresses; inside, The People of Freedom has already split, and the ministers who stayed with the government he abandoned have formed a party of their own. He refounds Forza Italia under its first name and goes into opposition holding no seat in either chamber.
stops.quote: Even people who hate him, and there are a lot of them, want to read and hear about him.
stops.quote_source: Erin Burnett, Erin Burnett OutFront, CNN, 26 February 2013; a remark about Berlusconi, not by him
suggested_refs: The Senate vote of 27 November 2013 under the Severino law
sources: Contemporary Italian and international press coverage of the November 2013 Senate vote

stops.name: Tribunale di Milano, the verdict undone
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day; the Cassation confirmation of the acquittal follows in March 2015, month attested and day not recorded
stops.campa: The Milan court of appeal takes the Ruby verdict apart: the abuse of office, it rules, does not exist, and paying El Mahroug is not a crime, because he could not have known her age. In March 2015 the Court of Cassation makes the acquittal final and his eligibility for office comes back. Meanwhile the divorce from Veronica Lario, who said in 2009 that she would not stay with a man who consorts with minors, has been settled against him at a figure reported near forty-eight million dollars a year.
suggested_refs: The Milan appeal judgment of 18 July 2014 and the Cassation confirmation of March 2015

stops.name: Massandra winery, above Yalta, the bottle from 1775
stops.date_confidence: the trip runs 11 to 12 September 2015; the research pool had placed it at Foros, about 30 km from either documented stop, and that location is rejected
stops.campa: He flies into Crimea with Vladimir Putin, eighteen months after Russia annexed it, and the two are shown through the excavated Greek city at Chersonesus in Sevastopol and then down into the cellars at Massandra above Yalta. A bottle of jerez laid down in 1775 is opened for them, and Ukrainian prosecutors will open an embezzlement case over it. Kyiv bans him from the country. He holds no office of any kind, and he has just recognised an annexation with nothing but his body.
suggested_refs: The Massandra winery cellars and the 1775 jerez bottle opened during the September 2015 visit

stops.campa: He sells AC Milan to Rossoneri Sport Investment Lux for 830 million euros, closing thirty-one years. The club took five European Cups under him. He is eighty years old, out of parliament, with two months of his ban still to run, and he has just parted with the only thing he owned that filled a stadium with people singing. Fininvest keeps the television. The Sunday audience, which he assembled before he ever assembled a party, now belongs to men whose names the crowd will not learn.

stops.campa: The ban has run out, and at eighty-two he stands for the European Parliament and is elected in the May vote, taking his seat when the term opens in July. Forza Italia is under nine per cent, third inside its own coalition behind Matteo Salvini's League and Giorgia Meloni's Brothers of Italy. He walks back into the chamber he first entered in 1999, when he led the opposition and the largest party on the Italian right was his. He is now the ancestor of a right that has outgrown him.

stops.campa: Nine years after being thrown out of it, he is returned to the Senate as senator for Monza and takes his seat under a government led by Giorgia Meloni, whose party was a fragment of a fragment the first time he took office. He is eighty-six. A hot microphone catches him describing letters and twenty bottles of vodka he says he has exchanged with Putin, and he is made to put his position on the invasion of Ukraine in writing. The 2013 vote is not mentioned by anyone in the room.

stops.name: San Raffaele Hospital, Milan, half past nine in the morning
stops.date_confidence: attested to the hour
stops.campa: He dies at half past nine in the morning at the San Raffaele in via Olgettina, where he has been treated through years of chronic myelomonocytic leukaemia. He is eighty-six. He has been prime minister three times across nine years, tried in more than thirty proceedings, definitively convicted once, expelled from parliament once, returned to it once. Forbes puts the estate at 6.8 billion dollars. The Council of Ministers declares a day of national mourning and orders the flags to half mast for three days.

stops.name: Duomo di Milano, the state funeral
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day
stops.campa: The state funeral is held in the cathedral in the Ambrosian rite by Archbishop Mario Delpini: about two thousand three hundred inside, some fifteen thousand in the square, Mattarella and Meloni, four former prime ministers, Viktor Orban, Gianni Infantino. Giuseppe Conte stays away. Napoleon put the iron crown on his own head under this vault in 1805 and made himself King of Italy. The rector Tomaso Montanari refuses to lower his university's flag and calls the funeral a distortion of history. Applause carries the coffin out into the piazza.

stops.name: Tempio Crematorio Panta Rei, Valenza, the burning
stops.date_confidence: June 2023 attested; the exact day of the cremation is not given in the source and is set to the day of the funeral for ordering
stops.campa: The body is driven west out of Lombardy to the Panta Rei crematorium at Valenza and burned. No cameras follow it. Years before, he had commissioned Pietro Cascella to build him a tomb in the park at Arcore: a hundred tonnes of marble and travertine called Volta celeste, with a chamber underneath sized for himself and for whoever he chose to invite in. It never received the authorisations a burial place requires. It stands in the grass at the villa holding nobody, and it is holding nobody today.

stops.name: Chapel of San Martino, Arcore, the ashes come home
stops.date_confidence: June 2023 attested; the day of the interment is not given in the source and is set after the cremation for ordering
stops.campa: The ashes come back to Villa San Martino and are set in the chapel of San Martino inside the house, beside his parents Luigi and Rosa and his sister Maria Antonietta. The villa he bought in December 1974 from a family the newspapers had already destroyed holds him at the end: the library, the picture gallery, the park with the empty monument standing in it, and the small chapel that was authorised when the monument was not. A short drive north is Brugherio, where he laid out his first town for four thousand strangers.
